q.x: Noclip did an interesting documentary about GOG. "GOG: Preserving Gaming's Past & Future" [link]

desc:
How do old games come back from the dead? We talk to the people at GOG (https://www.GOG.com) about the work they do to hunt down & release classic games, and their mission to encourage more DRM free releases.

Noclip's work is 100% crowdfunded. Consider supporting us on Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/noclip

Check out our new website here: www.noclip.video
Buy merch here: https://store.noclip.vi

recs.x:
lat price in all geos, the ones who can't afford it will invest more time in pirating the software. As a side effect, piracy is normalized in those communities as a necessary way of life in the digital world. Naturally, their tools and methods will leak out to other communities and make piracy easier in places that CAN afford them. Devs would rather sell to those communities at a "loss" than ostracize them and deal with the fallout.
